findings.title: Remains, capacity, and an appointed term
findings.claim: The focus's bones and pulverized remains meet the next ayah's creation of the cosmos, explicit capacity to create their likeness, and appointed term: material decay is placed within a future act the passage calls possible and time-bound.
findings.mechanism: The focus names the resistant material state and asks about being raised into a new creation. In 17:99, repeated creation, capacity, likeness, and a term answer that material objection; its refusal and no-doubt wording also frame the response as resistance to an announced event. The preceding gathering and recurring fire keep recompense in the immediate frame.
findings.reader_payoff: The remains remain the concrete subject, while the surrounding passage makes their re-creation intelligible as an appointed act rather than an event whose limit is set by the body's present state.
findings.containment: Bodily resurrection remains the plain subject. The sending facet is retained only as a bounded directional resonance toward an appointed event; no task, destination, material process, or detailed mechanism is supplied.

epistemic.reason: The channel evidence and 17:99 context directly support capacity, likeness, and a fixed term. The dispatch facet is more peripheral and is stated only as a bounded contextual resonance.

findings.title: Recompense as an embodied counterpart
findings.claim: The deictic recompense can be read beside 17:97's gathering of the deniers blind, mute, and deaf: refusal of the signs is met by a bodily closure of seeing, speech, and hearing.
findings.mechanism: The focus names denial of the signs, then quotes a spoken objection; the immediately preceding ayah gathers the same group with impaired sight, speech, and hearing. Those conditions meet the focus's signs, denial, and speech as a reciprocal bodily counterpart.
findings.reader_payoff: Recompense becomes legible as an embodied answer to non-reception, not only as a consequence named after the fact.
findings.containment: The sensory states may also be punitive attributes without a strict one-to-one mapping to each act of denial or speech. The correspondence is contextual and attributed, not a claim about the deniers' private intentions.

epistemic.reason: All six trace coordinates and roots match the supplied focus and 17:97 occurrence projection. The fit between each sensory condition and a chosen act remains an attributed interpretation.

findings.title: A recompense that renews its intensity
findings.claim: Because 17:97 says the fire is increased whenever it subsides, the focus's deictic recompense can include an iterated process in which each decline is answered by renewed intensity.
findings.mechanism: The root occurrence for recompense in 17:98 follows the explicit whenever-subsiding/increase/blaze sequence in 17:97. That recurrence makes the recompense readable as an ongoing counteraction rather than only a fixed state.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the previous verse's repetition as part of what the focus points back to when it names their recompense.
findings.containment: The recurrence is one detail within the prior fate, not a lexical definition of recompense or a claim that every aspect of judgment follows this loop. The reciprocal connection note also allows the prior verse to supply the underlying rejection while adding little imagery.

epistemic.reason: Each traced focus/context coordinate matches the packet. The extension from the fire cycle to the functional shape of recompense remains an attributed contextual reading.

findings.containment: This does not replace bodily resurrection with a theory about identity. Likeness may state equivalent creative capacity while ordinary same-person resurrection remains intended; the exact basis of continuity is left open.

findings.title: Denial beside a relabeled sign
findings.claim: The Moses passage supplies a bounded parallel for the focus's denial: explicit signs and acknowledged insight are followed by Pharaoh's magic label, making active redescription of evidence newly visible as one possible shape of rejection.
findings.mechanism: The focus names denial of signs and quotes an objection. In 17:101-102, clear signs and insight are placed beside Pharaoh's claim that Moses is bewitched and Moses's reply that Pharaoh knows the signs are insights from God. Their contact lets the focus's denial be read against a local example of evidence being rhetorically relabeled.
findings.reader_payoff: Denial can be seen as a way of answering evidence with a counter-description, not only as a failure to encounter evidence.
findings.containment: The parallel does not establish that the focus's speakers privately recognized the signs or that their resurrection question is itself a lie. Pharaoh's claim to knowledge may also be rhetorical; the focus's quoted question remains intact.

epistemic.reason: The 17:101-102 coordinates and roots align exactly, but transferring their rhetorical operation to the focus remains an attributed analogy. The specialized false-attribution branch on the focus speech verb is excluded.

findings.title: Fragments and paced differentiation

The later revelation passage joins truth and recitation with separation into portions, measured reading, and progressive delivery; that process image meets fragmentation with ordered differentiation and a whole still available across parts.

findings.containment: The revelation's delivery is an analogy, not an asserted physical model for resurrection or a claim that the passage intends the same process in both domains. An alternative reading leaves the domains unrelated.

epistemic.reason: All listed focus and contextual coordinates match the packet, but the relation between paced revelation and bodily re-formation is explicitly an attributed cross-domain analogy.

findings.mechanism: The focus sets remains against new creation. In 17:100, guarded stores, withholding for fear of expenditure, and human narrowness form a concrete scarcity pattern; that human model meets the focus's material objection as a possible projection onto creative power.
findings.reader_payoff: The objection can be heard as reasoning from human limits about storage and spending, rather than as a measure of the Creator's capacity.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory projection, not a stated motive or doctrine. The 17:100 passage may concern human miserliness without addressing resurrection, and the focus's bodily question remains fully live.

epistemic.reason: Every 17:100 coordinate and focus return matches the supplied packet, but transferring its human resource economy to the resurrection objection is explicitly speculative.

findings.containment: This does not establish that the speakers sincerely believe their question, that it is false speech, or that the later speakers answer them directly. The question remains quoted as asked, and the false-attribution specialization is excluded.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch and 17:101-102 coordinates match the packet, but activating supposition through the reported question remains an attributed contextual reading and does not settle the speakers' stance.

findings.mechanism: The focus's denial of divine truth is the carrier. External 1:6 asks God to guide 'us' to the straight path, and 1:7 identifies that path against anger and misguidance. The first-person request meets the focus's rejection and adds a participatory response absent from the native pericope reading.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's account of denial now sits beside the reciter's own request for guidance, without identifying the reciter with either group.
findings.containment: This is an external recitation overlay, not a claim that 1:6-7 directly explains 17:98 or that the request proves the focus's speakers knew the signs. It adds a first-person posture while leaving the native findings intact.

epistemic.reason: The external words and focus carrier are exact packet evidence; their participatory contrast is a bounded inference created only in Phase 2.
